title: Research
text:
Current research

Hellinger Criteria for Uniqueness and Dynamic Uniqueness in Infinite-Memory Shift Systems
Master’s research in probability theory
University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Brazil · 2026
The project studies compatibility and uniqueness of probability laws for systems with infinite memory, including chains with complete connections and related shift systems. It lies within probability theory, with connections to ergodic theory and dynamical systems.
Poster: 3rd Workshop on Combinatorics, Number Theory and Dynamical Systems, Fortaleza, Brazil, 19–23 October 2026.


SPDE for Spatial Data with Censored and Missing Responses
Research in spatial statistics
Escuela Superior Politécnica del Litoral (ESPOL), Ecuador
Likelihood-based inference and spatial prediction for data with censored or missing responses, using stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) to model spatial dependence.

title: Research
text:
Research experience

Methodology for Post-Selection Inference in Regression Models
Research Assistant
Facultad de Ciencias Naturales y Matemáticas (FCNM), Escuela Superior Politécnica del Litoral (ESPOL), Ecuador
September 2023–August 2024
Conditional inference for penalized robust regression under a multivariate Gaussian model, conditioning jointly on variable-selection and outlier-detection events. Work included truncated Gaussian inference for linear functionals, numerical approximation of truncation sets, and selective \(p\)-values, with simulation studies for Huber–Lasso and exponential-loss regression.


Multivariate methods and dimensionality reduction
Research Assistant
Center for Statistical Studies and Research, ESPOL, Ecuador
February–April and August–December 2024
Low-dimensional representations of multivariate data using t-SNE and projection-based methods, including a graphical construction for simultaneous representation of variables and taxonomic units. Application to agricultural practices among small-scale farmers in the northern Ecuadorian Amazon.

title: Research
text:
Research software

SPDEcensSpatial
R package · ESPOL, Ecuador · August 2024–January 2025
R implementation of SPDE-based spatial models for inference and prediction with censored or missing responses.
View repository on GitHub ↗


IA2RMS R Implementation
Research software · ESPOL, Ecuador · October 2023–January 2024
Implementation of the Independent Doubly Adaptive Rejection Metropolis Sampling (IA2RMS) algorithm of Martino, Read, and Luengo in R, including its use within Gibbs sampling schemes for conditional distributions in multivariate models.
View repository on GitHub ↗

title: Pablo Zúñiga
text:
I’m Pablo, from Ecuador, and I now live in Campinas, Brazil. I came to mathematics through statistics, and my studies have gradually drawn me toward probability theory and more abstract mathematical questions. I’m currently pursuing a Master’s in Statistics at the University of Campinas (UNICAMP).
What I enjoy most about research is following a question far enough to understand the ideas behind it. These days, that often means thinking about randomness, memory, and the structures that govern a stochastic process.
I also care about communicating science: explaining why a question is worth asking, what research helps us understand, and how fundamental research can contribute to technology and society. I enjoy football and music, too.

title: Pablo Zúñiga
text:
Research
My main research interests lie in probability theory, particularly the compatibility and uniqueness of probability laws, stochastic systems with infinite memory, and ergodic phenomena in measurable dynamical systems. Further interests include stochastic differential equations and interactions between probability and statistics.
Current work concerns probability laws for systems with infinite memory. I also work on spatial inference using stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) for data with censored or missing responses.
